claims.text: TaVCrW is a refractory high-entropy alloy.
The initial TaVCrW state is a disordered solid solution at 0 K.
An MTP trained on GGA-PBE energies and forces can replace the EAM reference potential for TaVCrW.
FEP using a multi-stage lambda schedule can replace thermodynamic integration for computing the solid-liquid free-energy difference.
The substitution of EAM plus TI by MTP plus FEP will reduce computational cost by more than 80%.
The MTP plus FEP melting-temperature prediction will be within 10 K of the TOR-TILD baseline.
The FEP solid-liquid free-energy difference will agree with the TI result within 0.5 meV/atom.
Accurate reproduction of the ab initio phase-space distributions of both liquid and solid phases is the structural mediator enabling rapid FEP convergence.
Capturing local atomic environments and short-range order allows the MTP to reproduce the relevant free-energy landscape.
The MTP is a computationally efficient surrogate for the DFT potential-energy surface and can generate the large ensembles required for FEP.
FEP bypasses the slow convergence of TI by evaluating the free-energy difference through intermediate perturbation states.
Short-range order contributes approximately 2-3 meV/atom to stabilization.
Electronic density-of-states gap effects influence the melting point.
A supercell containing at least 128 atoms is required to sample the SRO contribution adequately.
The validation temperature range must cover 2000-2400 K to sample the liquid fully and capture the melting transition.
High-temperature magnetic fluctuations are neglected in the initial MTP training.
Neglected magnetic fluctuations can be accounted for through a post-hoc electronic-entropy correction.
GGA-PBE underbinding or overbinding errors for V and Cr at 0 K may propagate into the liquid free energy.
FEP convergence for liquids with strong SRO may depend on the lambda schedule and the quality of the MTP training data.
A matched comparison against TOR-TILD on a simpler benchmark alloy can test melting temperature, solid-liquid free energy, computational cost, and liquid SRO.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and mechanism require the MTP to capture electronic-excitation effects, whereas the conditions describe those effects as an external electronic-entropy correction rather than something represented by the trained MTP.

The conditions state that magnetic fluctuations are accounted for by an electronic-entropy correction, while the boundary only assumes that they are negligible or can be corrected; the actual treatment is therefore not specified consistently.
